summary: Pakistan's online visa system says it is open to citizens of 192 countries and that the six GCC countries are not required to apply for a visa; its tourist visa page says citizens of GCC countries do not require a visa to enter Pakistan. The Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi lists its requirements for a visit visa, with a fee of Rs. 120 per entry for Indian citizens.

currencyLimits.text: The State Bank of Pakistan's general permission lets travellers to Pakistan bring foreign currency notes without limit (except un-issued notes and coin). Pakistani currency notes are limited to Rs 10,000 per person at any one time when brought in from or taken out to any country other than India, and Rs 3,000 for India. Any person may take out foreign currency up to USD 10,000 per visit above 18 years, USD 5,000 from 5 to 18 years and USD 1,000 up to 5 years (or the equivalent); a person not ordinarily resident in Pakistan may also take out the unspent foreign currency they brought in, if their continuous stay has not exceeded three months.

tips.text: Pakistan's visa portal says online applications for Pakistan's visa can only be submitted at https://visa.nadra.gov.pk and that it has no collaboration with any other website. For a tourist entry visa it lists a photograph, passport and hotel booking details.

The UK FCDO says you must obtain advance permission from local or federal authorities to travel in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan and several districts in Azad Kashmir, that there are several prohibited areas across the country, particularly around military installations, and that in areas of higher risk local authorities sometimes arrange police escorts.

TravelHealthPro says travellers who intend to visit Pakistan for four weeks or more should be aware that proof of polio vaccination recorded on an International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), given 4 weeks to 12 months before departure from Pakistan, may be required on exit, and that failure to produce an ICVP may result in vaccination on departure.

The UK FCDO says to dress modestly: men and women should cover their shoulders and legs in public, and women should cover their heads when entering mosques and holy places, and in rural areas. During Ramadan it says not to eat, drink, smoke or chew gum in public in the daytime, including in your car.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Pakistan?
faq.answer: Pakistan's visa portal says citizens of GCC countries do not require a visa to enter Pakistan, and that the online visa system is open to citizens of 192 countries. Its fee calculator asks for the country you are applying from; for a tourist/visit visa (individual, less than 3 months, single entry) it gives USD 20 for an application from Algeria and USD 60 for one from the United States. The Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi lists its requirements for a visit visa, with a fee of Rs. 120 per entry for Indian citizens.

faq.question: How long does the Pakistan eVisa take?
faq.answer: Pakistan's visa portal gives the processing time for a tourist entry visa (individual, up to 3 months) as 7-10 working days, and 4 weeks (working days) for Afghanistan and Somalia passport holders. If the application is sent back to you for review, the processing time re-starts from the date you resubmit it, and the application stands cancelled if you do not resubmit it within seven days.

faq.question: Can Indian citizens visit Pakistan as tourists?
faq.answer: The Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi lists its requirements for a visit visa: among them, copies of a Visa Information Form with information on each place to be visited, a notarised or attested invitation from a sponsor in Pakistan for each city to be visited, and a fee of Rs. 120 per entry for Indian citizens. No official source we could read says whether tourist visits are granted.

faq.question: Can I enter Pakistan on an Israeli passport?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states whether Pakistan admits travellers on Israeli passports.

faq.question: Is Pakistan safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to within 10 miles of the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan, to Balochistan Province and to listed areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province, and against all but essential travel to Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

entryRequirements.customs.notes.0.text: Importing alcohol or pork products is illegal. You could be detained if you try to import them.

entryRequirements.customs.notes.1.text: Penalties for possession, use or trafficking of illegal drugs are severe. Convicted offenders can expect the death penalty, jail sentences, heavy fines and/or deportation.

countryFacts.payments.text: The economy is primarily cash based. Credit cards are accepted by some larger establishments. Currency can be exchanged at all international airports. ATMs are available in main cities but may not accept foreign debit cards.

countryFacts.safety.text: FCDO advises against all travel to Balochistan Province.
FCDO advises against all travel to within 10 miles of the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
FCDO advises against all travel to these areas in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province:
FCDO advises against all but essential travel to Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
There is an ongoing risk of terrorism.
You or your travel agency should contact the local authorities of your destination in advance to check the local security situation.

In areas of higher risk, local authorities sometimes arrange police escorts for your own protection. They will also tell you if you need a No Objection Certificate from the Pakistani Ministry of Interior.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: Pakistan can experience flooding and landslides during monsoon season which is usually from late June to early October. The flooding can affect all provinces in Pakistan.

The north of Pakistan is mountainous. Many roads, including the N15 highway between Chilas and Babusar in Gilgit Baltistan, are inaccessible at some times of the year due to extreme weather conditions.

countryFacts.driving.text: Convention on Road Traffic Vienna, 8 November 1968
You’ll need to have both the 1968 version of the international driving permit (IDP) and your UK driving licence with you in the car.
You should carry an International Driving Permit.

visaTypes.tourist-embassy.feeNotes.text: Deposit/credit slip for the applicable visa fee (Rs. 120/- per entry for Indian citizens) credited to RBL Bank, Vasant Vihar Branch, New Delhi
The fee could also be paid by credit/debit card at the High Commission, New Delhi (an Additional 3% to be charged on account of Bank processing charges).

entryRequirements.overstay.text: Do not overstay the duration of your visa. You could face legal action or be banned from further entry into Pakistan. The status or nature of your visa cannot be changed while in Pakistan. If your visa has expired, you may be able to apply for an exit permit online.
Authorities may stop you from boarding your flight if your visa has expired. You could also face heavy penalties, including fines and detention.
If your visa has expired, contact the Ministry of Interior for an exit permit.
